messages:
cheng: Heads up — during calypso-v2 int8 bring-up we started seeing detok split on ordinal phrases like '第1次' -> '第 1 次'. Small but consistent BLEU/chrF regression on zh->en eval set :bug:

anya: reproable locally? can you paste the minimal example and the tokenizer output? :thinking:

cheng: minimal repro below. model=calypso-v2, quant=int8, tokenizer from repo at HEAD. Note this is with the same vocab we use for hosted endpoints.

```
# input
src = "我们今天是第1次演习。"

# tokenization (expected)
# ['我们', '今天', '是', '第1', '次', '演', '习', '。']

# tokenization (observed after int8 bring-up)
# ['我们', '今天', '是', '第', '1', '次', '演', '习', '。']

# detokenized (expected) -> "We are holding our first drill today."
# detokenized (observed) -> "We are holding our 1 st drill today."
```

eval-bot: nightly-eval/calypso-v2-int8 zh->en: BLEU 24.7 -> 22.6 (delta -2.1), chrF -3.2. Triggered by ordinal and date/numeric slices.

sam: interesting. could be a tokenizer normalization or merge rule change. any recent merges to tokenizers/normalizer?

cheng: I ran a quick bisect across tokenizer commits. The split appears after commit a1b2c3f which touched unicode normalization tables and ZWSP handling. The token ids and merges didn't change, but the pre-tokenization normalization now inserts a tiny gap for mixed digit+han sequences.

anya: oh. that explains the whitespace insertion at detok stage. are we sure quant itself didn't change decode behavior? maybe KV cache path or rounding of whitespace tokens?

cheng: I checked model logits and decode logits are identical modulo a few whitespace tokens. So root cause looks tokenizer normalization + detok merge behavior interacting with token merging rules in the pre-tokenizer. Quant makes the evaluation delta visible because the numeric/ordinal slice is sensitive.

lisa: workaround idea — add a detok post-process rule that collapses patterns like `第\s*([0-9一二三四五六七八九十百千万]+)\s*次` -> `第$1次` until we fix upstream. quick regex and add to our detok pipeline in serving runtime.

sam: can we also add a small eval slice to prevent regressions: azhar/locale-ordinals slice? Add to ci-evals with threshold chrF/BLEU guard.

cheng: yep. I'll open two PRs: 1) revert/adjust the problematic normalization in tokenizers (or pin the tokenizer submodule for calypso-v2 bring-up), 2) add the detok postprocess as short-term mitigation in console/serving (patch applied only for zh locales). Also adding the eval slice to nightly.

anya: thanks — can you include the minimal repro curl we can run against hosted sandbox? put in PR description.

cheng: sure. example curl: ```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"calypso-v2-int8","input":"我们今天是第1次演习。","detok":"default"}'
```

cheng: I'll also attach a small test set of 120 zh ordinal sentences (1..100 + chinese numerals + dates) and run bisect job results in the PR. plan to revert tokenizer change for bring-up if CI fails.

eval-bot: created issue #4321: "zh ordinal detok regression — calypso-v2-int8" and queued nightly bisect job.

lisa: good plan. thanks for catching this early — ordinals are common in our translation workloads. :thumbsup:

anya: assigning to cheng, tagging eng-ml and eng-ml-tokenizers. please update when PRs are ready.

cheng: will do. quick temporary mitigation deployed to staging (detok postprocess). regression on staging reduced to BLEU delta -0.1.

anya: perfect. keep us posted.
